en: The Low Triplet, etc., and the Root Pair.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root and not-root, a state with a middle root arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Nine [conditions] in the case of root;
... six in the case of resultant; ... nine in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root and not-root, a state with a root that is fixed in rightness arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition (*hetu*), nine; ... pe ... in the case of resultant condition (*vipāka*), three; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), nine.
Dependent on a state that does not have the Path as its object and is not a root, a state that has the Path as its object and is a root arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. In the case of root condition, twenty-six; ... pe ... in the case of repetition condition (*āsevana*), fifteen; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition, twenty-six.
A non-arisen state that is not a root-cause is not a condition, by way of root-condition, for an arisen state that is not a root-cause.
A state that will not arise and is not a root-cause is not a condition, by way of root-condition, for an arisen state that is not a root-cause.
Non-arisen states that are not root-causes and states that will not arise and are not root-causes are not conditions, by way of root-condition, for an arisen state that is not a root-cause.

Condition. (Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: six; under predominance: three; under conascence, mutuality, and dependence: three; under strong-dependence: six; under postnascence, resultant, faculty, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance: three.
